In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, even if the proposed dataset is the first of its kind, it still has some shortcomings and that the results of the evaluation show that the task of cross-language textual detection is still an open problem.
the best performing method for cross-language textual similarity is the one using the best performing machine translation system, which is Google Translate.

the best performing methods are those based on the use of word embeddings, with the exception of the cross-language similarity detection task where a method using a combination of word embeddings and word alignments is the best.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a dataset which is multilingual, contains cross-language alignments for different granularies, and is based on both paralell and comparable corpora.

we have built a dataset which is the first of its kind and which can be used for the evaluation of various cross-language text similarity methods, and that we have shown that the performance of the state-of-the-art methods is not sufficient for real-world applications.
our dataset is the most comprehensive and challenging dataset for the evaluation and development of cross-language textual detection methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of the cross-language alignment has a great impact on the performance of the similarity detection system.

a multilingual dataset is needed to evaluate cross-language textual similarity methods and that a dataset with multiple granularities is needed to assess the impact of the granularity of the similarity detection.
cross-language textual similarity methods are still far from being able to detect cross-lingual similarity with the same level of precision as monolingual similarity detection methods.
